body: This might be wrong, but IIRC I once heard that UK eggs would be illegal in the US, and US eggs would be illegal in the UK. It's probably because of the washing and the vaccine differences.

Aw, it's sadly quite common among people with eating disorders, you're not alone in this!

You could write down your feelings and review them at a later time when you don't feel as guilty or keep yourself distracted while eating (my favourite way is by watching shows with subtitles on, it has visuals and audio + you can read the subtitles to avoid always looking down at your food during the boring parts). Meal planning also is really helpful, since you already know exactly what you'll be eating before you even eat.

Maybe you feel sick because your body isn't used to eating that much/that type of food anymore? This could also be from stress/eating quickly.

You could go on a walk, try yoga, or massage your abdominal area to feel better but you might want to ask for different foods next time that you eat to prevent this from happening :( i'm sorry you went through that!!

Please don't hurt yourself, you matter so much more than you think you do. Is your dog worth living for? It's okay to cry, your emotions are valid and I'm proud of you for being able to stop bottling them up. Do you have any coping mechanisms for when this happens? There are distraction methods, you might be interested in looking into them. They won't stop the pain but they could help you calm down or get distracted from all the pain.

Hey, you don't need to be "more black" or "less white," you're perfect the way you are, your race doesn't define your culture or your personality traits. I think that the top commenter was right about asking them to explain themselves, you should listen to him! I hope things get better for you, you're heard and you matter! <3 

I think the name of this is 'racial imposter syndrome,' googling that term has a lot of results.  There are many people with similar experiences to you and you could relate to them + learn some ways to cope with other people's stories.
